sensorSource: Deterministic synthetic DeviceMotion/DeviceOrientation events at 16 ms in browser pages
checks: Play requests sensors during user activation, then the leader starts bowling without setup, Ready or Arm buttons
Fast sideways aim reaches the real TV guide in both directions despite hand acceleration, without releasing a ball
A backswing and return to rest do not release a bowling ball
A forward swing and wrist twist produce one bounded, authenticated roll; extra motion cannot duplicate it
Backgrounding cancels an unfinished swing and foreground requires fresh motion, without another permission prompt
Sensor gaps discard partial deliveries; a fresh opposite wrist turn produces the opposite curve
The phone switches sports, starts table tennis and routes fresh sensors across visibility changes
Touch controls remain one tap away during motion play
Denied sensor access falls back automatically to playable touch controls
The lobby waits for the first phone to choose Start game
Granted permission without real gyro readings falls back to touch instead of leaving the player in setup
limitations: Sensor permission API is mocked; real iOS/Android permission dialogs are not tested.
No physical phone axis/grip quality, haptics, motion-to-display timing or full game acceptance is established.
